record_verbatim.evidence: FB2-SAF-SEC-000005's safety_allocation.safety_goal_ref is 'FB2-SAF-SCO-000001'. No artifact with that id exists in either profile. The corpus's safety-case skeleton is FB2-SAF-SCS-000001. The reference is also self-contradictory with the field's own prose: the mitigation text says 'traced to the project's safety-case skeleton' and the standard_id is ISO_26262_2018 rather than an argument record, so the value appears to be a mistyped safety-case id. The reference sits inside a required field of the requirement schema (safety_allocation.safety_goal_ref), which is a free string and so accepted a typo the link registry would have caught had the value been expressed as a link.
record_verbatim.impact: The requirement whose reference is broken is the one covering entropy and third-party component governance, and it is the requirement this pass had the least verification leverage over: its own rationale records that the observed source derives the initial sequence number from a single 32-bit state seeded with a build-time literal, and that an ungoverned component set is an open item. A requirement in that position whose safety allocation points at nothing cannot be traced into a safety argument by a reader who follows the field. The defect is invisible to the link validator because the value is not a link: it is a string inside a required payload field, and no check resolves strings in payload fields.
